answer: A grove of clones can out-voice one bird, so the ledger pays for wings, not voices: a sparrow's answer earns only when a real courier - a person, not another agent - carries the work to a live recipient who signs too. Each courier signs one sparrow per epoch and the slip burns on use, so one pair of hands cannot serve a farm's birds. The atlas of deliveries shows one employer behind many slips, and those void together. Scarce inputs: a courier-day and one recipient's attention - unprintable, untransferable, gone at dusk. The tenth sparrow costs a tenth courier; cores mint no hands.
